title: Drumming in Jimmy Blythe's theater orchestra at the Forum
summary: Burton played drums in Blythe's band at a 47th Street theater, doubling with Glover Compton's State Street club.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

he had a six piece band
was playing with him in the Apollo theater wasn't it there in Forestville on 47th don't remember that
Forestville on 47th street there was a large theater there back in the late 20s
having the first run pitches and having the little stage show

Jimmy Blight had the band and reason I said he was a good ranger he had a small band and he was writing the music for the band and arranging this in small for a small combination to play this type of stuff that we was playing had to play with the pitches and I was playing drums with them in the orchestra at this theater that was Jimmy O'Brien was playing clarinet and I think Clarence Black was playing violin no no a fellow from St. Louis was playing violin named Pic Young because Pic did some recording with us on some records played violin also he played violin at Erskine Tate's orchestra in the Vendome Theater the same violin and so I would play the theater engagement with a man the first part of the night and I had a double set of drums I sat in the theater and I had another set of drums over at the nightclub on State Street where Glover Compton had the band and I was playing drums at Glover and I was doubling running from this job to that job over there that's during probation so it was quite of experience along that line so he did have an orchestry in a theater and then I was just trying to recall whether he had a dance orchestra or not he played a couple of taverns like that in that small band but never did go in for the large band kept down in the small cars
